first_impression.reaction: Fine, it isn't promising me anything, it's a list. I skipped the rings, went straight to the FAQ and the 'How to read this list' bit, then skimmed a few entries to see if the sourcing holds up. It mostly does. I'm not here for a planner though, so it was always going to be a skim.

journey.quote: Where outlets disagree on a detail, we have left it out rather than choose between them.
journey.reaction: Good. That's the first wedding blog I've seen admit sources conflict. Makes me trust the rest more.

journey.quote: You will notice there are no prices or valuations. That is deliberate: the figure tells you nothing about whether a style will suit the hand that wears it.
journey.reaction: Honest that it's a choice, I'll give them that. But I'm a numbers person, and leaving the numbers out isn't how I'd judge a ring. At least they point me to a separate spending guide.

journey.quote: According to the V&A, Prince Albert gave Queen Victoria an emerald ring in the shape of a serpent for their engagement.
journey.reaction: It names a source I can check. That's what I want.

journey.quote: Jewellery historian Marion Fasel identified it as a Jessica McCormack design, which is how it has been widely reported; the designer had not publicly confirmed this at the time.
journey.reaction: They tell me who said it and that it isn't confirmed. Not overclaiming. Good.

journey.quote: Most outlets describe the ring as an emerald-cut diamond on a thin band.
journey.reaction: Which outlets? Everywhere else you've named the source. Here it's just 'most outlets'. Small thing, but it's the sort of line I'd go and check.

journey.quote: One trade-off: a band set all the way round is difficult to resize, so get the size right before it is made.
journey.reaction: Actual trade-offs, not just 'it's gorgeous'. Same with the marquise points and the pearl. Useful.

journey.section: Sun, salt water and long-haul flights
journey.quote: Before you leave, check that the ring is covered by your insurance while travelling overseas, and keep a recent photograph of it with your travel documents.
journey.reaction: Practical. This is the only bit that's genuinely useful to me as a groom with a ring and an overseas wedding.

journey.quote: If the next one is where to marry, a Wedded Advisor can plan the venue, travel, vendors and payments, anywhere in the world, as your single point of contact from the first idea to the last dance.
journey.reaction: 'Payments' is the word that stops me. Is my money going through you? Do you take a cut from the venue? And 'from the first idea to the last dance' is brochure talk. Nothing here about what the Advisor costs.

unanswered_questions: How is a Wedded Advisor paid: flat fee, percentage, or commission from venues and vendors?
When the Advisor handles 'payments', do supplier prices include any mark-up?
Is there a real destination wedding I can see with the actual budget?

turn_offs_found.quote: as your single point of contact from the first idea to the last dance.
turn_offs_found.why: Emotional line where I wanted a fact about what the service includes and costs.

would_share_with: My fiancee, maybe, for the style table, not for the planner pitch

cta_reaction.quote: When you are ready to talk it through, Wedded Concierge is the place to start.
cta_reaction.why: The CTA comes after real evidence, which I respect, but it tells me nothing about the fee model or whether you take commissions. I'm comparing three planners and I'd rule out whoever makes me ask before I know what I'm paying for.

top_3_changes: In 'Where your ring goes next', add one plain sentence on how a Wedded Advisor is paid (and whether supplier prices carry commission), or link to a page that says it.
Replace 'from the first idea to the last dance' with something concrete about what the service actually covers.
Name the outlet wherever an entry falls back on 'most outlets' or a bare 'reported', for example the Sofia Richie Grainge entry, so the sourcing matches the rest of the list.

checks.check: Every journey point and turn-off has an exact quote from the draft
No invented brand facts; fee and commission gaps listed as unanswered questions

assumptions: Daniel would skim to the FAQ and method section first, per decision_behaviour; the 25 entries were sampled rather than read in full.
